test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 12 Nov 2021 Shift 1
subject: general
question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution declares that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty, except according to procedure established by law?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Article 21__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The major goal of** Article 21 is the Right to Protection of Life and Personal Liberty, **which is a right guaranteed against State Action as opposed to** violation **of such right by private individuals.
 
• The** Indian Constitution's Article 21 **was established by the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• **Article 21 specifically states** that a law must be in place before a **privacy violation may be justified. **For no one's life or personal** **freedom may be taken away from them without **following the legal process. **
 
• According to **Subhash Chandra Bose**, the right to social and economic fairness is a basic freedom protected by** Article 21. **According to the learned judge, **"status without means,** the right to life, and the dignity of a person were cosmetic rights. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International human rights organisation Article 19** aims to protect and advance freedom of speech and knowledge around the world.

 In** 1987,** it was created.
 
• Self-incrimination is prohibited by **Article 20 of the Indian Constitution**. "No individual accused of any offence shall be required to testify against himself," the** law states.**
 
• Titles are abolished according to** Article 18**. It specifies that the State shall not bestow any titles that are not** academic or military honours**. No **Indian national **may accept any titles from foreign governments.
